content: This review is an update of previously published reviews in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews from 2010 and 2013. Epithelial ovarian cancer constitutes approximately 90% of all ovarian cancer cases. Standard treatment typically involves debulking surgery followed by six courses of platinum-based chemotherapy, which achieves complete clinical remission (CCR) in up to 75% of cases. However, among those who achieve remission, 75% will experience a relapse within a median timeframe of 18 to 28 months, and only 20% to 40% of women survive beyond five years. Maintenance chemotherapy has been proposed as a strategy to prolong remission, but no systematic review has been conducted to evaluate its impact on epithelial ovarian cancer until now. The objective of this review was to assess the effectiveness and toxicity of maintenance chemotherapy for epithelial ovarian cancer and to evaluate its impact on quality of life (QoL). The original review involved a comprehensive search of multiple databases, including the Cochrane Gynaecological Cancer Review Group Specialised Register, CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase, PubMed, CBMdisc, CNKI, and VIP, up to May 2009. For subsequent updates, searches were extended to October 2012 and February 2017. The review also included information from ongoing trials, reference lists of published articles, and consultations with experts in the field. The selection criteria focused on randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that compared maintenance chemotherapy with no further intervention, maintenance radiotherapy, or other maintenance therapies. Two independent reviewers assessed the eligibility and quality of the trials and extracted data. The primary outcomes analyzed were overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS), which were treated as dichotomous variables. Toxicity and QoL data were also extracted when available. Analyses were conducted on an intention-to-treat (ITT) basis, and subgroup analyses were performed based on the type of drugs used. No new studies were identified for inclusion in this update. A total of eight trials involving 1,644 women were included in the review. When all chemotherapy regimens were combined, meta-analysis revealed no significant differences in three-year, five-year, or 10-year OS or PFS. For five-year OS, the combined risk ratio (RR) was 1.03 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.96 to 1.10; 4 studies, 899 participants; moderate-certainty evidence). For five-year PFS, the combined RR was 1.06 (95% CI 0.97 to 1.17; 3 studies, 761 participants; moderate-certainty evidence). Similar results were observed when trials of different chemotherapy regimens were analyzed separately. When comparing chemotherapy with radiotherapy, the only significant finding was for 10-year PFS in patients with pathological complete remission (PCR), where whole abdominal radiotherapy showed a favorable RR of 0.51 (95% CI 0.27 to 1.00). However, there were no significant differences in three-year or five-year OS rates between the two groups. The authors concluded that there is no evidence to support the use of platinum agents, doxorubicin, or paclitaxel as maintenance chemotherapy over observation alone. Further research is needed to investigate the potential effects of paclitaxel as a maintenance chemotherapy agent.
